# How is HTML interpreted

Day 2, 10:25 · Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations · coverage: transcript, slides

Speaker from a back-reference in a later talk ('Cherry already talked about the page ... main content'), heard in a second attendee recording. The author's recording starts mid-talk, so the opening is from slides only.

## Claims

- **[Slide]** A Google slide titled Data from Crawling showed an example of what the crawler passes on for processing: the fetch result, the connect time and the time to first byte in milliseconds, the robots policies that apply to the fetch, and the raw HTTP response with the page's HTML.
  <br><sub>`D2-C024` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Extends [D1-C063](../day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Extends [D1-C064](../day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Extends [D1-C092](../day1/D1-S10-how-google-thinks-about-crawl-budget.md) · Used by `DEV-PRF-01`</sub>

- **[Slide]** In Google's example fetch record, the robots policies that apply to a fetch, shown as the value opt-out-google-extended, travel with the fetched page into processing.
  <br><sub>`D2-C025` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [List of Google's common crawlers](https://developers.google.com/crawling/docs/crawlers-fetchers/google-common-crawlers) · Extends [D1-C086](../day1/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md) · Extends [D1-C064](../day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Extends [D1-C522](../day1/D1-S07-how-google-interprets-robots-txt.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** A Google pipeline slide placed processing between the crawler and the index and listed six processing steps: HTML parsing, rendering, deduplication, feature extraction, signal extraction and index selection.
  <br><sub>`D2-C026` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Extends [D1-C036](../day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Extends [D1-C063](../day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Extended by [D2-C128](../day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Repeated by [D2-C441](../day2/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) · Extended by [D2-C444](../day2/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md) · Extended by [D2-C688](../day2/D2-S20-deciding-what-goes-in-the-index.md)</sub>

- **[Slide]** The HTML parsing step turns a fetched page's HTML into a Document Object Model (DOM) tree of elements, attributes and text nodes.
  <br><sub>`D2-C027` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Used by `DEV-HTM-05`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google extracts every element of a page so that it can tell the header, the navigation and the main content apart, and a slide labelled the main content as very important.
  <br><sub>`D2-C028` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization) · Repeated by [D2-C309](../day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) · Extended by [D2-C868](../day2/D2-S07-understanding-what-s-on-a-page.md) · Extended by [D2-C474](../day2/D2-S12-what-is-structured-data-and-why-we-need-it-on-the-internet.md) · Used by `DEV-HTM-01`, the glossary term *Main content (centerpiece)*</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Make the main content of every template easy to separate from the header, navigation and footer, for example as one clearly delimited main area, because Google identifies the main content and treats it as the most important part of the page.
  <br><sub>`D2-C029` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted · Used by `DEV-HTM-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Besides the visible content, Google extracts elements that site owners add to the HTML, because they are useful for indexing and, for some of them, for ranking.
  <br><sub>`D2-C030` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works), [meta tags and attributes that Google supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/special-tags)</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google extracts the rel=canonical link, through which site owners state their preferred canonical URL, and uses it in deduplication and in canonical selection.
  <br><sub>`D2-C031` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [What is canonicalization](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/canonicalization), [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Extends [D1-C128](../day1/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extended by [D2-C379](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Used by `DEV-CAN-03`</sub>

- **[Slide]** The rel=canonical link element is placed in the head section of the HTML and tells Google that one page is the representative of another.
  <br><sub>`D2-C032` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [How to specify a canonical URL with rel="canonical" and other methods](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/consolidate-duplicate-urls) · Used by `DEV-CAN-03`, the glossary term *rel=canonical*</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google extracts hreflang annotations, through which site owners specify the language variants of their content, to know whether a page has an equivalent with similar content in another language.
  <br><sub>`D2-C033` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Tell Google about localized versions of your page](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions) · Extended by [D2-C382](../day2/D2-S08-handling-web-duplication.md) · Used by the glossary term *hreflang*</sub>

- **[Stage]** The speaker said that knowing a page's other-language versions from hreflang is useful in ranking.
  <br><sub>`D2-C034` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Tell Google about localized versions of your page](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/international/localized-versions)</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Put rel=canonical and hreflang link elements in the head of the HTML the server sends, not only in JavaScript-rendered HTML, so Google can read them during HTML parsing without depending on rendering.
  <br><sub>`D2-C035` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted · Used by `DEV-CAN-03`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Links and anchors are among the things Google extracts from a page's HTML, and the slide card for them simply read 'We like links.'
  > "We like links."
  <br><sub>`D2-C036` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works), [meta tags and attributes that Google supports](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/special-tags) · Used by `DEV-URL-01`</sub>

- **[Stage]** The speaker said links are still an extremely important part of the internet and of most major search and AI systems.
  <br><sub>`D2-C037` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google uses the links it extracts for three purposes: discovering new pages, determining a site's structure, and ranking.
  <br><sub>`D2-C038` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Link best practices for Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/links-crawlable), [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Extends [D1-C040](../day1/D1-S03-how-search-works-and-where-s-ai.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-01`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google can extract links written as an a element with an href attribute that holds an absolute or a relative URL, which the speaker called the good old normal way.
  <br><sub>`D2-C039` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Link best practices for Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/links-crawlable) · Used by `DEV-URL-01`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google cannot extract a link from an a element that only has an onclick handler, because Googlebot does not click, so the JavaScript is never triggered.
  <br><sub>`D2-C040` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Link best practices for Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/links-crawlable), [Pagination, incremental page loading, and their impact on Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/specialty/ecommerce/pagination-and-incremental-page-loading) · Repeats [D1-C115](../day1/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Extended by [D2-C184](../day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Extended by [D2-C287](../day2/D2-S06-what-is-google-friendly-javascript.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** Google cannot extract a link from an href attribute placed on an element other than a, such as a span, because that is not a standard way to make a link.
  <br><sub>`D2-C041` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Link best practices for Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/links-crawlable) · Used by `DEV-URL-02`</sub>

- **[Slide]** A Google slide also listed as not extractable an a element with a routerLink attribute instead of an href, and javascript: URLs such as javascript:goTo('products') or javascript:window.location.href='/products'.
  <br><sub>`D2-C042` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Link best practices for Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/links-crawlable) · Used by `DEV-URL-02`</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's link best practices say Google can generally crawl a link only if it is an a element with an href attribute, and list routerLink without href, href on a span, onclick-only a elements and javascript: URLs as not recommended, while noting that Google may still attempt to parse them.
  <br><sub>`D2-C043` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted · is the documentation · [Link best practices for Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/links-crawlable) · Used by `DEV-URL-01`, `DEV-URL-02`</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Google's link-extraction slide put routerLink, href on a span, onclick-only links and javascript: URLs under 'can not extract', which is stricter than Google's link documentation saying Google may still try to parse them; either way they are not dependable links for discovery.
  <br><sub>`D2-C044` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Audit every template and JavaScript component that outputs links, such as navigation, pagination, filters and product tiles: each needs a real a element with an href, because onclick handlers, routerLink without href, href on a span and javascript: URLs leave the target pages without a link Google can reliably extract.
  <br><sub>`D2-C045` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted</sub>

- **[Stage]** The speaker said Google sometimes also extracts URLs that are typed out as plain text on a page without being hyperlinked; the remarks around this point were unclear in the recording.
  <br><sub>`D2-C046` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Do not rely on plain-text URLs for discovery: even if Google sometimes picks them up, a proper a href link is what was described as feeding discovery, site structure and ranking.
  <br><sub>`D2-C047` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted</sub>

- **[Slide]** Links extracted during processing are sent back to the crawl queue, where scheduling starts again for the newly found URLs.
  <br><sub>`D2-C048` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Understand the JavaScript SEO basics](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/javascript-seo-basics), [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Extends [D1-C063](../day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Repeats [D1-C328](../day1/D1-S05-how-crawling-works.md) · Extended by [D2-C168](../day2/D2-S05-lightning-session-d-rendering-and-javascript.md) · Repeated by [D2-C442](../day2/D2-S11-finding-the-gold-nuggets-structured-data-media-and-more.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** The robots meta element is also extracted when Google processes a page's HTML, and the speaker called it probably one of the most important extracted elements, or one the audience is probably interested in.
  <br><sub>`D2-C049` · Day 2, How is HTML interpreted (Cherry Prommawin, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Block Search indexing with noindex](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/block-indexing), [Robots meta tag, data-nosnippet, and X-Robots-Tag specifications](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/robots-meta-tag)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's page on valid page metadata says that once Google detects an invalid element in the head, it assumes the head has ended and stops reading further elements there; only title, meta, link, script, style, base, noscript and template elements belong in the head.
  <br><sub>`D2-C831` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, How is HTML interpreted · is the documentation · [Use valid HTML to specify page metadata](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/valid-page-metadata) · Used by `DEV-CAN-03`, `DEV-HTM-05`</sub>
